newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger opposition stages protest march.
newsitem.headline: Niger opposition stages protest march.

text.p: At least 2,000 opposition supporters in Niger turned out on Saturday demanding restoration of democracy and the rule of law in the West African nation, witnesses said.

The march, organised by women's groups, followed the release of opposition leaders and militants detained after police on January 11 broke up a banned march called to demand greater access to state media.

An eight-party opposition alliance boycotted November legislative elections accusing President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara of rigging a July presidential poll to legitimise his rule after a January 1996 coup.
Mainassara ordered the release of detained opposition leaders and supporters on Thursday, saying he wanted to promote national reconciliation and a broad-based government.
One of those detained was Mahamane Ousmane, the civilian president Mainassara ousted.
Saturday's marchers also demanded the release of opposition lawyer Souley Oumarou, who was arrested on Friday, and former national assembly member Sala Habi.
Mainassara supporters won 59 of the 83 seats in the national assembly in the legislative election.
Former colonial power France and the United States, which has condemned Mainassara's election as fraudulent, had urged the release of the three opposition leaders.
